import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
    nums = list(map(int, data.split()))
    nums.sort()
    if nums:
        sys.stdout.write('\n'.join(map(str, nums)))
        sys.stdout.write('\n')

main()

act.result: Built sortints.py as pure Python: reads all of sys.stdin.buffer, splits on whitespace, maps to ints, list.sort(), writes '\n'.join(map(str, nums)) plus a trailing newline. bench.py generates fixed-seed data (data_200k.txt, data_1m.txt), verifies correctness by comparing parsed output against sorted reference on the 200k case (printing 0 on any mismatch or nonzero exit), then times three runs over 1,000,000 ints and prints 1/best_seconds. Verified: correctness passed and fitness printed ~1.73 (i.e., ~0.58s for the 1M-int workload). A second equivalent tweak (guarding the empty-list case) scored comparably (~1.78), so pure Python with read+split+map(int)+sort+join is retained as the fastest simple approach; no separate division was warranted within the remaining step budget since the variant itself was already the chosen approach and bench.py confirms both correctness and speed.
